findings.summary: Documents four tiers economy|standard|strong|max; FR-021 adds advanced between standard and strong while keeping old plans semantically stable.
Floor table and routing text assume four tiers; entry point is size-budgeted so five-tier and catalog guidance must replace text, not append.
States logical tiers are economy, standard, strong, max; needs advanced plus F1-F5/L1-L5 alias normalization language.
model_tier appears only in an example; there is no documented value set, alias rule or MODEL_MATRIX reference, so advanced and aliases need an explicit contract.
Public tier table lists four tiers and the provider table omits Muse, GLM and DeepSeek; README.pt-BR.md mirrors both and must change in step.
Requires reading exactly one of two provider files (Codex, Claude); FR-006..008 add Muse, GLM and DeepSeek profiles with their own MODEL_ROUTING_<PROVIDER>.md.
Concrete ids live in routingctl CURRENT_MODELS (map v2026-09-30-v6) and the tables must match it; the catalog must bootstrap from this map to keep NFR-001 compatibility and not duplicate ids.
CURRENT_MODELS re-applied on every run overrides stale ids; catalog refresh and invalid-model recovery must define precedence against this fixed map.
States concrete model ids live in the per-plan orchestrator.config.json; FR-004/005 move resolution provenance to a plan-local MODEL_MATRIX snapshot without changing TODO semantics.
Version-2 overlay and tier_routes are keyed by four tiers; advanced and absent optional providers (FR-026) need schema, configure and doctor treatment without breaking v1/v2 files.

findings.section: 3. Run mapped validations under the watcher
findings.summary: Evidence JSONL under .ai-work/resource-watch persists past plan cleanup and section 2 keeps log cursors across retries; FR-034 requires owner/scope, retention policy and deterministic removal.
Says resource-monitor reports are preserved by cleanup and reset; FR-034 keeps only deliberate shared state such as SERVICE_MAP.md or retention-policy evidence.

findings.section: 6. Escalate from classified evidence / Validation stagnation
findings.summary: No-progress rule uses output/CPU progress on POSIX but only signature aging on Windows; FR-028 forbids elapsed-time-only stall classification, so the Windows path needs explicit evidence or a documented limit.
Worker report has no failure-evidence, delegation, usage or cache fields; FR-027/030/031 additions must be optional and versioned because this schema also validates current workers.

findings.section: 3. Elevate by delegation. Never switch the root session
findings.summary: Existing rules never switch the root, run at most two read-only explorers, and give assistants no authority; FR-024/025/029 delegation roles must extend these bounds, not relax them.

findings.section: 3. Split deterministically before asking a model to summarize
findings.summary: Immutable SHA-256 fragments and anchors already exist (preplanctl); FR-032 retrieval refinements should build on them and not introduce a second fragment store.

Unreleased section records concrete model ids and feature lists; every new contract (catalog, aliases, providers, cleanup) needs an entry and package version policy should be followed.
